svg.title: Stonehallow - master site plan
svg.text: the royal castle on its crag
A sprawling medieval port-city that grew without a plan
Surveyed for The Warden of the Stones - a living world of 4.1 km x 4.1 km, ready to build in 3D
• Thin lines join ground of equal height (10 m)
• Every 1 px of the heightmap = 1 metre
Contour: 10 m here, 1 m on detail sheets
Nobody planned Stonehallow. It began as a ferry where the River Wend splits around King's
Isle, among standing stones and burial mounds far older than memory. Fishermen came for the
estuary, monks for the island, a warlord for the crag; each built where it suited them, and
the lanes grew between like roots. The old places were never cleared away: the Moot Hill
still rises in the Grand Market, the Kingstone still stands where two roads meet, and the
Three Kings' Table sits on the Minster lawn.
Five hundred years on, the city spills over three walls and two riverbanks to the sea. Cogs
unload at King's Quay, soldiers drill at the Star Citadel, scholars argue on the hill,
crowds pack the Great Auditorium and the fair field, and the King looks down on all of it
You are The Warden of the Stones. Your house faces the Kingstone. The ancient places are
yours to keep - and every one of them has a secret.
4 096 m x 4 096 m · sea level 20 m
